chapter_theme: The poet's modesty before the assembly (அவையடக்கம்): no one knows the Lord's greatness or the root of the nameless flame, and Tirumular disclaims the skill of those who sing, dance and seek; yet the Lord can be known by those who contemplate him, though even sages and gods may miss the fruit of the knowledge of tattvas.

95.reading: Who knows the greatness of our Lord? Who knows his breadth and length? I tell of my not knowing the root of the one great nameless flame.
95.nuance: பேரறியாத may mean 'nameless' or 'whose name is unknown'. The great flame (பெருஞ்சுடர்) whose root is unknown recalls the fire column of 88. Sengalvaraya lists Tevaram parallels asking who knows his nature.

96.reading: I do not know how to sing in the way of those who can sing, nor dance in the way of those who can dance, nor seek in the way of those who can seek, nor search in the way of those who can search.
96.nuance: The four skills may be the forms of devotion (song and dance) and of inquiry (seeking and searching). The disclaimer is conventional in a preface, but here it covers both worship and knowledge.

97.reading: Those who honour him with abiding words of truth, even Brahma who afterward made the world, can come to know the Lord who rises within sweet music by contemplating him.
97.nuance: The syntax is loose: Brahma may be one of those who know him, or a contrast (even the creator must contemplate). உன்னும் (contemplating) is the verse's way to knowledge, against 95's 'who knows?'.

98.reading: The knowledge of the tattvas was told at the foot of the mountain; the sages and gods who waited there for release, staying apart and praising, do not know this fruit through devotion alone.
98.nuance: தாழ்வரை (foothill, slope) may be the place where the teaching was given, perhaps Kailasa. The last line is the hard part: பத்திமையால் இப்பயன் அறியாரே may mean they do not know the fruit by devotion, or that because of their devotion they do not know it (they praise rather than understand). Either way it seems to rank knowledge of tattvas above praise alone.

links.note: 88 tells how Brahma and Vishnu could not find the foot and crown of the column of fire; 95 turns the same flame into the poet's own confession that he does not know its root.

96 disclaims: 'I do not know how to sing in the way of those who can sing, nor dance' (பாடவல்லார் நெறி பாட அறிகிலேன் ... ஆட). 2093 (repeated at 2559) asks what gain there is for those who cannot sing (பாடகில்லார்) what he did, beside those who can dance (ஆடவல்லார்). The poet's modesty in the preface uses the very lack the later verse treats as fruitless.

97 says the Lord rises within sweet music (இன்னிசை உள்ளே எழுகின்ற ஈசன்) and can be known by contemplation. 31 says the poet loved the one who took to singing sweet music in melody (பண்ணகத்து இன்னிசை பாடலுற்றான்). Both place the Lord in music, once as the one known there, once as the singer loved.

98 says the sages and gods who praise apart do not know this fruit through devotion (பத்திமையால் இப்பயன் அறியாரே), on the reading that ranks tattva knowledge above praise. 284 says the siddhas never discerned the light, but to devotees who bowed in devotion (பத்திமையாலே பணிந்து) he stood before them and gave release. On that reading the two make opposite claims about what devotion alone reaches.
